# Thunderbolt eGPU on Linux for local LLM inference

> What it takes to run an NVIDIA GPU in a Thunderbolt/USB4 enclosure on Linux and have Ollama use it, distilled from a September 2026 RTX 5080 / Razer Core X V2 / ASUS NUC 15 Pro (Arrow Lake, Thunderbolt 4, Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, driver 610-open) debugging session and the kernel, NVIDIA, ASUS and community sources it leaned on. Covers how the PCIe tunnel is built and why the Linux thunderbolt driver's host_reset rebuilds it, the kernel parameters that keep the BIOS tunnel (host_reset=0, realloc=off, clx=0), hotplug BAR sizing versus decode failures, a driverless MMIO chip-ID probe with per-hop Unsupported-Request localisation, NVIDIA driver blocking and power-management options for an eGPU, a systemd loader ordered after bolt, how to prove Ollama is on CUDA, and the ASUS iSetupCfg BIOS CLI. For anyone whose eGPU enumerates but reads 0xffffffff; verified-as-of 2026-09-24.

## PCIe tunneling over Thunderbolt 4 and USB4

- [Facts: PCIe tunneling over Thunderbolt 4 and USB4](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#pcie-tunneling-thunderbolt-usb4): 5 source-anchored facts from 2 sources
- [llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc](https://llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc/): On the NUC 15 Pro's Thunderbolt 4 ports the Core X V2 link negotiated 40 Gb/s (2 lanes x 20 Gb/s) per boltctl (4 facts)
- [github.com/CachyOS/linux-cachyos](https://github.com/CachyOS/linux-cachyos/issues/1057): CachyOS issue #1057 documents JHL9480 (Barlow Ridge) PCIe hierarchies disappearing when the tunnel runtime-suspends on 7.x kernels — workaround power/control=on via udev (1 fact)

## Linux thunderbolt driver: host_reset, CLx and bolt authorization

- [Facts: Linux thunderbolt driver: host_reset, CLx and bolt authorization](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#linux-thunderbolt-driver-host-reset): 7 source-anchored facts from 5 sources
- [llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc](https://llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc/): thunderbolt.clx=0 disables the USB4 CL0s/CL1/CL2 low-power link states. (3 facts)
- [kernel.org/doc/html](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/thunderbolt.html): boltctl list shows the enclosure's authorization state and negotiated rx/tx speed; the domain security level is in /sys/bus/thunderbolt/devices/domain0/security (1 fact)

## Diagnosing a GPU that has fallen off the bus: config space, MMIO chip ID and AER

- [Facts: Diagnosing a GPU that has fallen off the bus: config space, MMIO chip ID and AER](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#egpu-fallen-off-bus-diagnosis): 15 source-anchored facts from 2 sources
- [llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc](https://llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc/): A function-level reset (echo 1 > reset), a secondary bus reset through the downstream port, a 30-second enclosure AC power cycle (14 facts)
- [docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors](https://docs.nvidia.com/deploy/xid-errors/index.html): NVRM Xid 79 is 'GPU has fallen off the bus' and Xid 143 is a GPU initialisation error. (1 fact)

## PCI hotplug resource assignment: hpmmiosize, realloc and BAR placement

- [Facts: PCI hotplug resource assignment: hpmmiosize, realloc and BAR placement](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#pci-hotplug-resource-assignment): 5 source-anchored facts from 3 sources
- [llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc](https://llms-explorer.com/blog/thunderbolt-egpu-rtx-5080-linux-nuc/): Raising hpmmiosize made assignment succeed (3 facts)
- [kernel.org/doc/html](https://www.kernel.org/doc/html/latest/admin-guide/kernel-parameters.html): pci=hpmmiosize=N and pci=hpmmioprefsize=N set the non-prefetchable and prefetchable MMIO windows Linux reserves below each hotplug bridge (1 fact)

- [Facts: Ollama CUDA detection and GPU verification](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#ollama-cuda-verification): 5 source-anchored facts from 1 sources

## ASUS NUC BIOS Thunderbolt options and the iSetupCfg CLI

- [Facts: ASUS NUC BIOS Thunderbolt options and the iSetupCfg CLI](/t/thunderbolt-egpu-linux/llms-facts.txt#asus-nuc-bios-isetupcfg): 9 source-anchored facts from 8 sources
- [kmpic.asus.com/images/nuc](https://kmpic.asus.com/images/nuc/iSetupCfg-User-Guide.pdf): iSetupCfg cannot modify items on the BIOS Performance page, the Secure Boot page, the Add-In Config page, or the BIOS/HDD/TCG passwords, whatever the export shows. (2 facts)
- [asus.com/support/faq](https://www.asus.com/support/faq/1052633/): iSetupCfg is AMI's AMISCE, shipped by ASUS as the 'NUC Firmware Integrator Tool' (version 20260106 for NUC15CRK-B, inside the Aptio V Integrator Tools bundle). (1 fact)
- [winraid.level1techs.com/t/request-asus-nuc-15-pro-plus-rebar-enable](https://winraid.level1techs.com/t/request-asus-nuc-15-pro-plus-rebar-enable/117427): The NUC 15 Pro setup UI exposes no Above 4G Decoding, Resizable BAR or PCIe-tunneling option (1 fact)
